conclusion: The only literature item carrying a '20-30%' figure for DFT errors that could be traced is Perry et al., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147, 26865 (the original code tags it 'JACS2025_DFT_wrong_dominant_frac'). It reports that periodic DFT models give the wrong qualitative STABILITY ORDERING OF TAUTOMERIC CRYSTAL POLYMORPHS in ~20-30% of the surveyed cases, against a DLPNO-CCSD(T1)-corrected reference. It is not a solution-phase benchmark, uses no implicit solvent, no Tautobase and no experimental tautomer ratios, so it is not a band of 'solvated density-functional treatments' of dominant-tautomer misranking. The manuscript gives no citation for the band. The band must therefore be treated as UNVERIFIED in its current wording (reported to the user; the text is not rewritten here).
